title: Hof deployment plan
description: hofctl plan's output contract - a typed, ordered operation list plus the desired diff and observed drift it was computed from. Never a shell string: every operation is a fixed action type with typed fields, per the reconciler's 'no generic shell endpoint' rule in PLATFORM-OPS-PLAN.md.

planId.description: sha256 of the plan's own inputs+baseline, deterministic - never includes a timestamp, so a future hofctl apply can reject a plan whose inputs changed underneath it.

executable.description: false when blockers is non-empty - apply must refuse a plan that isn't executable.

operationId.description: A three-digit sequence prefix (this plan's own execution order) plus a descriptive suffix - unlike volume/service identifiers, operation ids legitimately start with a digit.

units.description: Keyed by hof.unit (the actual Compose service key), not by catalog artifact - Wachter's API and its agent share one artifact but are two units, and collapsing them loses one entirely.

configFingerprint.description: sha256 of this unit's own full rendered Compose service definition (image, environment, labels, volumes, ...) - catches a domain/CORS/browserPush/TLS-driven env change even when the image itself didn't change.

schemaVersion.description: Present only for a service with a catalog database entry - the release lock's declared schema version for its database component (from/to, see the catalog schema).

baselineState.description: The last-applied state this plan is diffing from - either loaded from /var/lib/hof/state, or the synthetic empty baseline (mode: bootstrap, generation: 0, installationId: null) on a truly clean host.

topologyDigest.description: sha256 over the rendered topology, backup config, and Caddyfile together - the one field that catches a change (like a backup schedule edit) with no per-unit Compose footprint at all.

desiredState.description: What services.yml + the catalog + the release lock render to right now - a plain snapshot, not itself a generation.

kind.description: manual-change: observed doesn't match the last-applied baseline for a resource desired still wants. missing: a managed resource baseline expects is gone from Docker. unmanaged: a resource matching this installation's naming exists but carries no hof.managed label, or belongs to a different installationId entirely. generated-missing: a generated file baseline recorded a checksum for is positively confirmed gone - repairable by config.write. generated-modified: a generated file's live checksum no longer matches what baseline recorded - someone hand-edited it; never silently overwritten. generated-unreadable: a generated file baseline recorded a checksum for exists but couldn't be read even with sudo - genuinely unknown whether it's missing, modified, or untouched; never auto-repaired, --repair-drift or not.

condition.description: Only for readiness.wait - what actually counts as ready for this specific unit. Most units have a real Compose healthcheck and must reach "healthy"; the gateway deliberately has none (see render-topology.mjs's own comment on why), so it only ever waits for "running".

argv.description: Only for database.migrate - the catalog's own database.command for this component, so an approved plan is self-sufficient and apply never has to re-interpret the catalog to know what to run.

volume.description: Only for database.migrate/backup.create - the catalog's own database.volume (or the volume backup.create is protecting).
